pulls.title: Accept SPIFFE bundle key use values under AS-configured trust
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Key Source Selection required an eligible key's `use`, if present, to be `sig`. SPIFFE trust bundles label JWT signing keys `"use": "jwt-svid"` (SPIFFE Client Authentication §6.1). An AS therefore could not configure a SPIFFE bundle endpoint as an attester's key source, although the Client Metadata section presents that bundle endpoint as the model for the configured key source.

Under AS-configured attester trust, the eligibility bullet now also accepts a `use` value the AS has configured for that key source as identifying signature keys, for example `jwt-svid` for a SPIFFE trust bundle. The exception is bounded by configuration the AS already holds, not by an outside document. Publisher-authorized key selection keeps the plain `sig` rule, because there the publisher chooses the key location.

Found in the Client Instance Assertion coverage audit. CIA's re-minted mode could use a SPIFFE bundle as its key source; without this change that path had no successor.

No keyword change: the ordered BCP 14 sequence is identical (51).

pulls.title: Align language and tone with published OAuth RFCs
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
A language and tone pass so the draft reads like the published OAuth RFCs (9449, 8693, 9068, 7662, 8705, 9728) and ATTEST. It follows the conventions of the style pass merged in draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-instance-id (PR #30), so the two drafts now match. There is no normative change. Each commit covers one kind of change and can be dropped on its own.

## Proof of no normative change

Checked against main at ba756d9:

- **Keywords:** the ordered BCP 14 sequence is identical with whitespace collapsed (51 keywords, same census). `noop_check.py` reports a difference only because some "MUST NOT" pairs now wrap differently across lines.
- **Conditions:** I checked every keyword sentence that now opens a paragraph. Each either already opened one with different wording (mostly "the AS" becoming "the authorization server"), or states its condition in the same sentence.
- **Unchanged:** all 10 fenced blocks and every existing anchor. Eight anchors were added for the new subsections.
- **Build:** clean, with no unresolved or uncited references and no rendered lines over 72 columns. The one new idnits warning is noise on the table-of-contents lines for the appendices.
- **Reworded normative sentences:** same party, condition, behavior and keyword. The notable ones:
  - The Errors definition list is now two paragraphs, each opening with its condition ("When the Client Attestation is the client authentication method, the authorization server MUST respond ... with the `invalid_client_attestation` error code").
  - "The attester MUST include:" now lists the `iss` claim, the `sub` claim, and the `kid` JOSE header parameter.
  - "applicable trust policy" is now "applicable key-trust policy".
  - The 404/410 removal rule now gives the status codes with their reason phrases.
- **Length:** 6110 to 6710 words (+10%); 25 to 27 pages. About 180 of the added words come from spelling out "authorization server" 93 times. The rest come from the new section headings, naming fields by kind, the error-condition sentences, and example lead-ins.

## What changed

- **Mechanical:**
  - "AS" is spelled out in running text. The mode name "AS-configured attester trust" is kept, so "(AS)" is expanded once in the Introduction.
  - Citations read "Section N of [REF]".
  - Security Considerations has one subsection per topic, and Privacy Considerations is its own section. They open with pointers to Sections 12 and 11 of ATTEST and Sections 8 and 9 of CIMD, checked against ATTEST-11 and CIMD-02.
  - IANA has one subsection per registry and says "This specification requests registration".
- **Register:** figurative and persuasive wording is removed ("closes that gap", "reaches", "hand key selection", "silently", "deliberately", "thief", "no substitute"). "Intentionally leaves trust to deployments" now matches what Section 10.8 of ATTEST says: it is out of scope.
- **Fields named by kind:** for example "the `iss` claim", "the `kid` header parameter", "the `use` parameter" of a JWK, "the `invalid_client_attestation` error code", and HTTP status codes with reason phrases. `client_attesters` is now a "client metadata parameter", the term ATTEST Section 9 and RFC 7591 use.
- **Terminology:**
  - ATTEST is introduced by name at first use, as CIMD already was.
  - "client publisher" is now a definition.
  - "endorsement fails" is now "endorsement validation fails".
  - "fetch" is now "retrieve".

- **Examples:** each opens with "The following example shows ...". Appendix A is retitled "Client ID Metadata Document Example".

1. **bc5213e** replaces "speak for" with "attest for", which the layer diagram already uses. Drop it if "speaks for" was meant as the security term of art.
2. **d52fb6a** turns the Introduction's two questions into "whether ..." clauses and keeps the two-question structure. Drop it to keep the question marks.
3. **Not done; each would renumber sections or change requirements:**
   - Rename "AS-configured attester trust" (for example "server-configured attester trust").
   - Split "Conventions and Trust Model", which holds normative subsections.
   - Merge the two overlapping `invalid_client_attestation` MUSTs in Errors.
   - Make "this profile" and "this specification" consistent where nothing contrasts with ATTEST.
   - Reword "configured entry" in the Key Source Selection MUST NOT; it is a condition of that requirement.

pulls.title: Resolve pre-publication review findings
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Resolves the pre-publication review of main at 5f6baa3. That review ran five parallel checks: two citation fact-checks (ATTEST; CIMD, SPIFFE-OAUTH and the RFCs), a security directorate read, an implementer read, and a document-consistency read. The i-d-template submission gates also ran. Every finding was checked against the draft and the cited text before being accepted. There is one commit per finding.

## Changes

| Finding | Commit | Change |
|---|---|---|
| RFC 7592 update: the "omit `client_attesters` from stored metadata" option would carry out an unauthorized removal | 57c9009 | **Normative.** An update the authorization server does not accept is rejected, or the stored value is kept (Section 2.2 of RFC 7592 lets a server ignore a submitted value). An unauthorized request never removes a stored endorsement. |
| "extends that option" contradicted the MUST NOT on the client's own `jwks_uri` (introduced by #32) | 51e2d9c | ATTEST §10.8's client-metadata option is applied through endorsed locations, not the client's own `jwks_uri`. |

pulls.title: Require invalid_client_attestation wherever ATTEST permits it
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Closes gap F from the pre-publication review (#33).

## The problem

ATTEST Section 7.4 says `invalid_client_attestation` "MAY be used in addition to the more general `invalid_client`" when:
- the attestation or its proof cannot be verified;
- the attestation key and the proof key do not match;
- the proof method is not supported.

This draft already requires `invalid_client_attestation` for endorsement failures, but a server could still answer a bad signature with `invalid_client`. The error code alone would then show whether endorsement validation passed, and so which attesters and key sources the server trusts. That conflicts with "the response MUST NOT expose policy details", which #34 extended to both uses of the attestation. It also makes the existing sentence "the code does not distinguish endorsement failures from other attestation failures" untrue.

## The change

One new MUST in Errors: except where the selected proof method's own specification requires a different error code (see Review follow-up), the authorization server MUST use `invalid_client_attestation` rather than `invalid_client` wherever Section 7.4 of [ATTEST] permits it, so that the error code does not reveal whether endorsement validation succeeded.

- **Why this is a safe narrowing:** it turns ATTEST's MAY into a MUST for exactly the failures ATTEST lists. It picks an option ATTEST already offers rather than departing from it, so ATTEST Section 13's limits on what a profile may change do not apply.
- **Codes left alone:** the codes ATTEST requires for specific cases (`use_attestation_challenge`, `use_fresh_attestation`, and DPoP's `use_dpop_nonce`). They ask the client to retry and reveal no trust policy.

## Review follow-up

- **f688b85:** errors required by the selected proof method's own specification take precedence. In DPoP combined mode, ATTEST Section 7.3 validates the DPoP proof "in accordance with [RFC9449]", and Section 5 of RFC 9449 requires `invalid_dpop_proof` for an invalid proof. The first commit's MUST would have overridden that. A DPoP proof failure reveals no trust policy, so the exception does not reopen the leak. A DPoP key that does not match the attestation's `cnf` claim (ATTEST Section 7.3, step 4) is an ATTEST check, and still produces `invalid_client_attestation`.
- **41b11a9:** RFC 9449 moves to normative references, because the MUST's exception now depends on its error code. It is Standards Track, so this adds no downref.

## Checks

- **Keywords:** 52 become 53. `normative_diff.py` shows one added keyword sentence and none removed. No keyword sentence newly opens a paragraph.
- **Build:** `make lint` is clean, the build succeeds, and no rendered line exceeds 72 columns.

The G items remain deferred to -01.
